As #HLPF2025 kicks off this week, the message is clear: Our Energy Future is Digital. 

Countries that integrate energy planning into digital strategies - and vice versa - will be best positioned to lead in both.
 
Digital, data and AI are reshaping how energy is produced, distributed and consumed. In doing so, they’re expanding access to critical services, powering local economies and strengthening climate resilience. In 2024, the Energy Transition Index rose by 1.1% - more than twice the average in the last three years - with countries in the Global South leading digital innovation across the energy value chain.
 
But the real opportunity lies in what the digital energy revolution can enable: from powering vaccine cold chains, to enabling digital agriculture, or unlocking access to the digital economy for women entrepreneurs. With the potential to reduce 5.4 GtCO₂e annually by 2035, AI can become central in low-carbon transitions, if deployed equitably.
 
By aligning national energy master plans, digital transformation strategies and investment frameworks, these solutions can become powerful drivers of systemic change to shape a more just and sustainable future.
